The quickest way to reach me is [mrenard@nus.edu.sg](mailto:mrenard@nus.edu.sg).
This page sets out what I can usefully help with, so you can tell in about a
minute whether it is worth an email.

---

## Research collaboration

I am most useful to a project that needs one of the following:

- **Statistical analysis of longitudinal or clustered data** — repeated
  measures, wearable and sensor streams, field studies where the same people are
  observed many times. Mixed-effects modelling, within/between decomposition,
  non-linear threshold estimation.
- **Exposure–response and threshold work** — where the question is not
  "is there an effect" but "at what point, and for whom".
- **Evidence synthesis done properly** — protocol development, PROSPERO
  registration, search strategy, risk of bias, and synthesis that survives peer
  review. I have registered four reviews and act as guarantor on one.
- **Turning findings into guidance** — translating modelled results into
  thresholds and advisory language that an agency can actually adopt.

I work across environmental physiology, sleep, public health and nutritional
science, and I am comfortable being the quantitative member of a team whose
subject expertise is elsewhere.

## Early career researchers

Much of my week is spent supporting teams of early career researchers — on
analysis planning, coding practice, interpretation and scientific writing —
across projects on dormitory heat and sleep, nighttime heat thresholds, cooling
interventions and heat vulnerability index development.

If you are working in heat, sleep or environmental physiology and are stuck on a
methods or analysis question, I am happy to talk. When you write, it helps
enormously if you include the question that interests you and why, rather than a
general expression of interest.

I also support early career researchers more broadly through the **NUS Medicine
Postdoctoral Association**, where I lead the Education Subcommittee, and through
the **Early Career Researchers Office**.

## Industry and institutional partnerships

I hold one of five Lead portfolios at the **NUS Medicine Early Career Researchers
Office**, with responsibility for **Strategic Partnerships, Business Development
and External Relations** (2026–27). In that role I represent the School's early
career researcher community in partnership discussions — placements, joint
programmes and industry-facing activity.

If you are at an organisation considering a partnership with NUS Medicine that
would involve early career researchers, this is a conversation I can start.

## Advisory and review work

I review for journals across sports medicine and environmental health, and I am
open to advisory work on heat-health guidance, protocol review and analysis
planning where I can add something specific.

## Media and speaking

My work on indoor heat and sleep has been covered in *The Straits Times* and
*Lianhe Zaobao*. I am glad to speak to journalists about heat, sleep and health
in tropical climates, and to give talks or workshops — particularly on
statistical methods for researchers who did not train as statisticians.

If you are writing about the work, the [heat and sleep explainer](heat-and-sleep.qmd)
has the findings in plain language plus a media kit — headshot, bios, and what I
can and cannot usefully comment on.

::: {.note-box}
**A note on what I will not be much use for.** I am not a clinician and cannot
advise on individual health. I do not take on analysis-only work with no
scientific involvement. And if a request needs an answer this week, please say
so in the first line — my calendar is usually the constraint, not my interest.
:::
